key_insight: Learn the dissipation potential with an input-convex neural network so the learned constitutive law remains physically well-posed, frame-indifferent, and dissipative by construction.
engineering_relevance: This provides a safer way to infer material models from indirect velocity data, improving stability and generalization for CFD and continuum-mechanics inverse problems.
method: ICNNE enforces convexity, frame-indifference, and evenness in the second strain-rate invariant via symmetrization.
A penalty at zero strain rate encourages dissipativity by pushing the potential gradient to vanish at the origin.
The inverse objective couples Firedrake finite elements with PyTorch to optimize the learned potential against velocity observations.
evidence_signal: The approach was tested on four cases—compressible Navier-Stokes, Herschel-Bulkley flow, Hibler sea-ice, and DEM data—and matched known physics, generalized to unseen geometries, and remained stable where unstructured methods diverged.
watch_item: The method depends on careful PDE-ML coupling and penalty tuning, so training cost and sensitivity to implementation details may affect robustness in new applications.
paper_title: Well-posed by Design: Learning Constitutive Laws from Velocity Data using Convex Neural Network Potentials
